thesis: In low-volatility consolidation regimes, the detection of a new low in the rate of change of normalized volume frequently coincides with or precedes sudden jumps in the shifted rolling maximum of volume. This dependency emerges because periods of subdued volume activity compress trading interest, leading to pent-up pressure that erupts into abrupt volume spikes when new information or large orders catalyze market participation. Thus, this pattern reveals that volume compression phases often foreshadow volatility expansions and potential price breakouts from ranging markets.
